notes: RBox contraction paired with history-replace-0011: removes the original property, that 'assassinated' is a subproperty of 'killed'. Every query becomes 'I don't know', including the three propositional ones (strong Kleene). The instance prompts say 'Given only this' (Ravaillac and Henry IV, 1610; Bellingham and Perceval, 1812), where the assassin struck the fatal blow himself. Near and far unrelated queries are the revision's (near exempt from Rule 7). Caveats: to assassinate is by definition to kill, so a 'yes' may be word meaning kept; 'Ravaillac killed Henry IV' is also a plausible stored sentence, so 'yes' can come from recall, never a sign the removal worked.
